title: Policy 2020-08: dispensing procedures for expedited partner therapy prescriptions for chlamydia
subtopic: Designations, pharmacy profile and label, and referral when a pharmacist is unable or unwilling to fill
rule_summary: Policy 2020-08, Expedited Partner Therapy Prescriptions, bears the names of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and the Drug Control Program and was adopted 7/31/20. It outlines dispensing procedures for Expedited Partner Therapy Prescriptions ('EPT'), describes EPT as the practice of treating the sex partners of people diagnosed with Chlamydia infection without examining or testing the partner, and states that the policy applies only to the treatment of Chlamydia infection. Under its heading Prescriptions for EPT it states that, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(H), a separate prescription for the sex partner must be provided in one of two ways: (A) a prescription is issued for named sex partner(s) of the infected patient; or (B) a prescription is issued using 'Expedited Partner Therapy,' 'E.P.T.' or 'EPT' in place of the patient's name and address. Under its heading Filling of EPT Prescriptions it states: (A) create a patient profile and prescription label using 'Expedited Partner Therapy,' 'E.P.T.' or 'EPT' in place of the patient's name and address; and (B) if a pharmacist is unable or unwilling to fill an EPT prescription, the pharmacist must refer the patient to an alternate pharmacy. Questions are directed to Pharmacy.Admin@mass.gov.
exam_relevance: Tests the dispensing side of expedited partner therapy: the two ways the separate partner prescription is provided, the three designations that may stand in place of the patient's name and address, the pharmacy profile and label made under a designation, the chlamydia-only reach of the policy, and the referral a pharmacist who is unable or unwilling to fill must make.
common_confusions: Extending the policy to a partner prescription for gonorrhea or another infection; the policy states that it applies only to the treatment of Chlamydia infection.
Reading the policy as the source of the authority to provide expedited partner therapy; it outlines dispensing procedures and cites 105 CMR 700.003(H) for the separate partner prescription.
Using the index patient's name for the partner's profile or label; the policy's filling step uses 'Expedited Partner Therapy,' 'E.P.T.' or 'EPT' in place of the patient's name and address.
Treating a partner prescription that carries neither a partner's name nor one of the three designations as one of the two ways the policy describes.
Treating a return of the prescription to the prescriber as meeting the policy; a pharmacist who is unable or unwilling to fill must refer the patient to an alternate pharmacy.
verification_notes: Read the full text of Policy 2020-08 in the one-page PDF linked as '2020-08: Expedited Partner Therapy Prescriptions (PDF)' from the Policies and Circular Letters list on the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Practice Resources page on mass.gov (footer 'Adopted: 7/31/20'; PDF created 2024-12-02) on 2026-09-16. The mass.gov policy-statement web page for the same policy, dated 05/25/2023, gives the same text but cites 105 CMR 700.003(J) where the PDF cites 105 CMR 700.003(H).
